item.title: Vouchers Prove Popular
item.description: A private school voucher plan, passed by state lawmakers, continues to exceed expectations. Comptroller Kelly Hancock says they’ve been overwhelmed by the number of parents who want to pull their kids out of failing public schools. More than 90-thousand applications have been submitted ahead of next week’s deadline. And he expects that number to get above 100-thousand.

item.title: Self Driving Trucks
item.description: Self-driving trucks are going further than ever before. A company called Aurora Innovation announced on their earnings call this week that their big rigs can now travel non-stop from Dallas to Phoenix. CEO Chris Urmson says human drivers cannot, under law, drive that far in one shift. The one-thousand-mile route takes about 15 hours to complete.

item.title: ICE Detention Center
item.description: San Antonio’s city council is being told that they cannot stop ICE from turning a warehouse into an immigrant detention center. Questions about whether power and water can be cut off were quickly shot down by City Attorney Andy Segovia. He says they’re required by law. The council was also told that tax dollars cannot be used to defend illegal immigrants in court.

item.title: Iran Oil Impact
item.description: Oil prices have been on a little roller coaster ride thanks to strained relations with Iran. Experts say there is the potential for disruptions when it comes to Middle Eastern shipments. Todd Staples, who heads the Texas Oil and Gas Association, called it a “short term disruption.” He says the good news is that domestic drilling has been hitting records. And that means you won’t see wild swings at the gas pump.
